$comment: Notes shown on the element pages (scripts/generate/gen-idml-reference.mjs). `Element@Attribute` is one element's note; `*@Attribute` is shared by every element that has the attribute, except those in `except`, and gives way to a description harvested from the chapters. A bare `Element` key holds that page's opening summary. `source` says what backs an entry: Paged's code (file:line), our chapters (`docs:`), the census or the local corpus, an InDesign probe, or `dtp` (general desktop-publishing knowledge). Never written from a vendor specification; leave out what those sources cannot back.

*@Self.note: The object's ID, unique within the document. An attribute that refers to this object holds this value.

*@Name.note: The name InDesign shows for the object in its panels. References between objects use `Self`, never the name.

Cell@Name.note: The cell's address, `column:row`, both counted from 0: `0:0` is the top-left cell.

Column@Name.note: The column's position in the table, counted from 0.

Row@Name.note: The row's position in the table, counted from 0.

*@DOMVersion.note: The version of InDesign's object model the part was written with, such as `20.0`.

*@src.note: The path, from the package root, of the part this entry pulls in.

*@ItemTransform.note: Places the object: six numbers `a b c d tx ty`, an affine matrix from the object's own coordinates to its parent's.

*@PathGeometry.note: The object's outline, in a `<Properties>` child: one path per contour, each a list of anchor points in the object's own coordinates.

*@ContentType.note: What the frame is meant to hold: `TextType`, `GraphicType` or `Unassigned`.

*@AppliedObjectStyle.note: The object style applied, by its `Self`, such as `ObjectStyle/$ID/[None]`. Attributes set on the object itself override the style's.

*@AllowOverrides.note: On a master page item: whether a page that uses the master may override it and edit it locally.

*@Visible.note: When `false`, the object stays in the document but is neither shown nor printed.

Condition@Visible.note: When `false`, text with this condition is hidden: it stays in the story but is neither shown nor printed.

*@Locked.note: When `true`, InDesign won't let the object be selected or edited. It still displays and prints.

*@Nonprinting.note: When `true`, the object shows on screen but is left out of printing and export.

*@LocalDisplaySetting.note: How InDesign draws this object on screen, overriding the view's display setting. It has no effect on output.

*@HorizontalLayoutConstraints.note: For liquid page rules: three tokens for the space to the left, the width and the space to the right, each `FixedDimension` or `FlexibleDimension`.

*@VerticalLayoutConstraints.note: For liquid page rules: three tokens for the space above, the height and the space below, each `FixedDimension` or `FlexibleDimension`.

*@FillColor.note: The swatch that fills the object (for text, its glyphs), by its `Self`, such as `Color/Black`. `Swatch/None` means no fill.

*@FillTint.note: The fill colour's strength as a percentage, 0–100. `-1` means no tint is set, the same as leaving the attribute out.

*@StrokeColor.note: The swatch the stroke is painted with, by its `Self`. `Swatch/None` means no stroke.

*@StrokeTint.note: The stroke colour's strength as a percentage, 0–100. `-1` means no tint is set, the same as leaving the attribute out.

*@StrokeType.note: The stroke style, by its `Self`, such as `StrokeStyle/$ID/Solid` or `StrokeStyle/$ID/Dashed`.

*@StrokeAlignment.note: Where the stroke sits on the path: centred on it (`CenterAlignment`, the default), inside it or outside it.

*@EndJoin.note: How the stroke turns at corners: `MiterEndJoin` (pointed, the default), `RoundEndJoin` or `BevelEndJoin`.

*@EndCap.note: How the open ends of a stroke finish: `ButtEndCap` (flat at the end point), `RoundEndCap`, or `ProjectingEndCap` (squared off half the stroke weight beyond it).

*@MiterLimit.note: For pointed corners, how far the point may reach, as a multiple of the stroke weight, before the corner is bevelled instead.

*@GapColor.note: The swatch painted in the gaps of a dashed, dotted or striped stroke. `Swatch/None` leaves them transparent.

*@GapTint.note: The gap colour's strength as a percentage, 0–100. `-1` means no tint is set.

*@OverprintFill.note: When `true`, the fill prints over the inks beneath it instead of knocking them out.

*@OverprintStroke.note: When `true`, the stroke prints over the inks beneath it instead of knocking them out.

*@LeftLineEnd.note: The arrowhead at the path's start: `None`, or one of InDesign's line ends such as `TriangleArrowHead`.

*@RightLineEnd.note: The arrowhead at the path's end: `None`, or one of InDesign's line ends such as `TriangleArrowHead`.

*@LeftArrowHeadScale.note: The size of the start arrowhead, as a percentage of its natural size.

*@RightArrowHeadScale.note: The size of the end arrowhead, as a percentage of its natural size.

*@ArrowHeadAlignment.note: Whether arrowheads stop at the path's ends or extend beyond them; every document in the census uses `InsidePath`.

*@GradientFillAngle.note: The direction of a linear gradient fill, in degrees. Used when the fill is a gradient.

*@GradientFillLength.note: How far a gradient fill runs from its first stop to its last, in points; for a radial gradient, its radius.

*@GradientFillStart.note: Where a gradient fill starts, as `x y` in the object's own coordinates.

*@GradientStrokeAngle.note: The direction of a linear gradient stroke, in degrees. Used when the stroke is a gradient.

*@GradientStrokeLength.note: How far a gradient stroke runs from its first stop to its last, in points; for a radial gradient, its radius.

*@GradientStrokeStart.note: Where a gradient stroke starts, as `x y` in the object's own coordinates.

*@CornerOption.note: The all-corner effect InDesign writes beside the four per-corner attributes (`None`, `RoundedCorner`, `InverseRoundedCorner`, `InsetCorner`, `BevelCorner` or `FancyCorner`). InDesign draws corners from the per-corner attributes alone, on page items and object styles: an element that spells its corners only here has square corners.
*@CornerOption.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@CornerRadius.note: The all-corner size, in points, InDesign writes beside the per-corner radii. It is not read, not even for a per-corner option that has no radius of its own (that corner is 12 pt).
*@CornerRadius.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@TopLeftCornerOption.note: The effect on the top-left corner, in `CornerOption`'s tokens; a bare `Rounded` or `Inset` is no effect. With the other three per-corner attributes, this is what InDesign draws.
*@TopLeftCornerOption.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@TopRightCornerOption.note: The effect on the top-right corner, in `CornerOption`'s tokens; a bare `Rounded` or `Inset` is no effect. With the other three per-corner attributes, this is what InDesign draws.
*@TopRightCornerOption.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@BottomLeftCornerOption.note: The effect on the bottom-left corner, in `CornerOption`'s tokens; a bare `Rounded` or `Inset` is no effect. With the other three per-corner attributes, this is what InDesign draws.
*@BottomLeftCornerOption.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@BottomRightCornerOption.note: The effect on the bottom-right corner, in `CornerOption`'s tokens; a bare `Rounded` or `Inset` is no effect. With the other three per-corner attributes, this is what InDesign draws.
*@BottomRightCornerOption.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@TopLeftCornerRadius.note: The size of the top-left corner's effect, in points; 12 when the corner has an effect and no radius.
*@TopLeftCornerRadius.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@TopRightCornerRadius.note: The size of the top-right corner's effect, in points; 12 when the corner has an effect and no radius.
*@TopRightCornerRadius.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@BottomLeftCornerRadius.note: The size of the bottom-left corner's effect, in points; 12 when the corner has an effect and no radius.
*@BottomLeftCornerRadius.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@BottomRightCornerRadius.note: The size of the bottom-right corner's effect, in points; 12 when the corner has an effect and no radius.
*@BottomRightCornerRadius.source: InDesign 20.0.1 DOM probes: core ADR 149 and tools/indesign-export/object-style-corners-probe

*@Applied.note: Whether this effect is switched on.

*@Opacity.note: How opaque the object or effect is, as a percentage: `100` is solid, `0` invisible.

*@BlendMode.note: How the object or effect combines with what lies beneath it: `Normal`, `Multiply`, `Screen` or another of the standard blend modes.

*@Size.note: How wide the effect's blur or bevel is, in points.

*@Noise.note: Grain mixed into the effect, as a percentage.

*@EffectColor.note: The swatch the effect is drawn in, by its `Self`.

*@UseGlobalLight.note: When `true`, the effect takes its light direction from the document's global light instead of its own angle.

*@AppliedFont.note: The font family, such as `Minion Pro`; `FontStyle` picks the face within it.

*@FontStyle.note: The face within the font family, such as `Regular` or `Bold Italic`.

*@HorizontalScale.note: Stretches the glyphs horizontally, as a percentage; `100` is the font's own width.

*@VerticalScale.note: Stretches the glyphs vertically, as a percentage; `100` is the font's own height.

*@BaselineShift.note: Moves the glyphs up (positive) or down (negative) from the baseline, in points.

*@Tracking.note: Even spacing added between all characters, in thousandths of an em.

*@Ligatures.note: Whether the font's standard ligatures, such as fi and fl, are used.

*@OTFContextualAlternate.note: Whether the font's contextual alternates are used (the OpenType `calt` feature).

*@AppliedCharacterStyle.note: The character style applied, by its `Self`, such as `CharacterStyle/$ID/[No character style]`.

*@AppliedParagraphStyle.note: The paragraph style applied, by its `Self`, such as `ParagraphStyle/$ID/NormalParagraphStyle`.

*@BasedOn.note: The style this one inherits from, by its `Self`. Any setting it leaves out comes from there.

*@SpaceBefore.note: Space added above the paragraph or table, in points.

ParagraphStyleRange@SpaceBefore.note:
Space added above each paragraph of the range, in points: every one of them has it, those after a `
` too. In a footnote it counts only between the note's own paragraphs.
ParagraphStyleRange@SpaceBefore.source: InDesign 20.0.1 probe: two 12 pt paragraphs of one range at 12/9 sit 35.4 pt apart; two one-paragraph notes asking for it sit one leading apart

*@SpaceAfter.note: Space added below the paragraph or table, in points.

ParagraphStyleRange@SpaceAfter.note:
Space added below each paragraph of the range, in points: every one of them has it, those before a `
` too. In a footnote it counts only between the note's own paragraphs.
ParagraphStyleRange@SpaceAfter.source: InDesign 20.0.1 probe: two 12 pt paragraphs of one range at 12/9 sit 35.4 pt apart; two one-paragraph notes asking for it sit one leading apart

*@GridAlignment.note: Whether the lines snap to a grid: `None`, `AlignBaseline` for the baseline grid, or a CJK frame-grid line such as `AlignEmCenter`.

*@BulletsFont.note: The font family the bullet character is set in.

*@BulletsFontStyle.note: The face, within `BulletsFont`, the bullet character is set in.

*@TextTopInset.note: The space between the cell's top edge and its text, in points.

*@TextBottomInset.note: The space between the cell's bottom edge and its text, in points.

*@TextLeftInset.note: The space between the cell's left edge and its text, in points.

*@TextRightInset.note: The space between the cell's right edge and its text, in points.

*@TextBefore.note: Text placed before the variable's value.

*@TextAfter.note: Text placed after the variable's value.

*@ColorEditable.note: Whether the swatch's colour can be changed in InDesign; built-in swatches such as Registration can't.

*@ColorRemovable.note: Whether the swatch can be deleted; built-in swatches can't.

*@KeyboardShortcut.note: The keyboard shortcut that applies the style in InDesign, encoded as a list of numbers. An interface setting; it does not change the text.

*@Label.note: Key–value data that scripts and plugins attach to the object, as `<KeyValuePair Key Value>` entries in a `<Properties><Label>` child. It does not change the layout.

*@EmitCss.note: When `true`, EPUB and HTML export writes CSS for the class this style is exported with. It does not change the page.

ParagraphStyle@SplitDocument.note: When `true`, EPUB export starts a new file at each paragraph that uses this style.

*@Capitalization.note: How the letters are shown: `Normal`, `AllCaps`, `SmallCaps` or `CapToSmallCap`. The stored characters keep their case.

*@Leading.note: The distance between baselines, in points, or `Auto` (the point size times the paragraph's `AutoLeading`). A line takes the largest leading among its runs.

*@KerningMethod.note: How automatic kerning is set: `$ID/Metrics` (the font's kerning pairs, the default), `$ID/Optical` (from the glyph shapes) or `$ID/None`.

*@Position.note: Superscript and subscript: `Normal`, `Superscript`, `Subscript`, or the font's OpenType forms `OTSuperscript`, `OTSubscript`, `OTNumerator` and `OTDenominator`.

*@AppliedLanguage.note: The text's language, such as `$ID/English: USA`. It picks the dictionaries used for hyphenation and spelling.

*@Skew.note: Slants the glyphs by this many degrees, a false italic; positive values lean right and `0` is upright.

*@KerningValue.note: Manual kerning at this position, in thousandths of an em, added to the automatic kerning.

*@StrikeThru.note: Whether the text is struck through with a line.

*@NoBreak.note: When `true`, the text is kept together on one line: no line break falls inside it.

*@PageNumberType.note: For a page-number marker (`<?ACE 18?>`) in the range: `AutoPageNumber` (this page), `NextPageNumber` or `PreviousPageNumber`; `TextVariable` marks a variable instance.

*@ParagraphBreakType.note:
On a range holding a paragraph mark (`
`): a break such as `NextColumn`, `NextFrame` or `NextPage` that moves the text after it; `Anywhere` is a plain paragraph end.
*@ParagraphBreakType.source:
dtp, census; corpus: on the CharacterStyleRange holding
, Anywhere/NextColumn/NextFrame/NextPage

*@AppliedConditions.note: The conditions applied to the run, as `Condition` ids separated by spaces. InDesign shows the run while any one of them is visible.

*@UnderlineOffset.note: How far below the baseline the underline sits, in points.

*@UnderlineWeight.note: The thickness of the underline, in points.

*@UnderlineColor.note: The swatch the underline is painted in, by its `Self`. It can also follow the colour of the text.

*@UnderlineTint.note: The underline colour's strength as a percentage, 0–100.

*@UnderlineType.note: The underline's stroke style, by its `Self`, such as `StrokeStyle/$ID/Solid` or `StrokeStyle/$ID/Dashed`.

*@UnderlineOverprint.note: When `true`, the underline prints over the inks beneath it instead of knocking them out.

*@UnderlineGapColor.note: The swatch painted in the gaps of a dashed, dotted or striped underline. `Swatch/None` leaves them transparent.

*@UnderlineGapTint.note: The underline gap colour's strength as a percentage, 0–100.

*@UnderlineGapOverprint.note: When `true`, the underline's gap colour prints over the inks beneath it instead of knocking them out.

*@StrikeThroughOffset.note: How far above the baseline the strikethrough line sits, in points.

*@StrikeThroughWeight.note: The thickness of the strikethrough line, in points.

*@StrikeThroughColor.note: The swatch the strikethrough line is painted in, by its `Self`. It can also follow the colour of the text.

*@StrikeThroughTint.note: The strikethrough colour's strength as a percentage, 0–100.

*@StrikeThroughType.note: The strikethrough line's stroke style, by its `Self`, such as `StrokeStyle/$ID/Solid`.

*@StrikeThroughOverprint.note: When `true`, the strikethrough line prints over the inks beneath it instead of knocking them out.

*@StrikeThroughGapColor.note: The swatch painted in the gaps of a dashed, dotted or striped strikethrough line. `Swatch/None` leaves them transparent.

*@StrikeThroughGapTint.note: The strikethrough gap colour's strength as a percentage, 0–100.

*@StrikeThroughGapOverprint.note: When `true`, the strikethrough's gap colour prints over the inks beneath it instead of knocking them out.

*@OTFFigureStyle.note: The digits used: `Default` (the font's own), or tabular or proportional with lining or oldstyle figures, such as `TabularLining` or `ProportionalOldstyle`.

*@OTFFraction.note: Whether the font's fractions are used, so that digits around a slash, such as 1/2, are set as one fraction (OpenType `frac`).

*@OTFOrdinal.note: Whether the font's ordinal forms, such as the raised letters of 1st and 2nd, are used (OpenType `ordn`).

*@OTFDiscretionaryLigature.note: Whether the font's discretionary ligatures, such as ct and st, are used (OpenType `dlig`).

*@OTFSwash.note: Whether the font's swash letterforms are used (OpenType `swsh`).

*@OTFTitling.note: Whether the font's titling alternates, capitals designed for large sizes, are used (OpenType `titl`).

*@OTFSlashedZero.note: Whether zero is set with a slash, to tell it from the letter O (OpenType `zero`).

*@OTFStylisticSets.note: The stylistic sets switched on, as one integer bit field: `1` is set 1, `2` set 2, `3` sets 1 and 2, and so on (OpenType `ss01`–`ss20`).

*@OTFHistorical.note: Whether the font's historical letterforms are used (OpenType `hist`).

*@OTFStylisticAlternate.note: Whether the font's stylistic alternates are used (OpenType `salt`).

*@OTFLocale.note: Whether the font's language-specific glyph forms are used for the text's language (OpenType `locl`).

*@OTFProportionalMetrics.note: Whether CJK glyphs use the font's proportional widths instead of their full-width em boxes (OpenType `palt`).

*@Justification.note: The paragraph's alignment, such as `LeftAlign`, `CenterAlign` or `ToBindingSide`; the justified `LeftJustified`, `CenterJustified`, `RightJustified` and `FullyJustified` differ in the last line.

*@LeftIndent.note: The space between the left edge of the column and the paragraph's lines, in points.

*@RightIndent.note: The space between the paragraph's lines and the right edge of the column, in points.

*@FirstLineIndent.note: The extra indent of the paragraph's first line, in points, measured from `LeftIndent`; a negative value makes a hanging indent.

*@LastLineIndent.note: An extra indent at the right end of the paragraph's last line only, in points.

*@Composer.note: The line breaker: `HL Composer` (Paragraph Composer, the default), `HL Single` (Single-line Composer), or their World-Ready forms `HL Composer Optyca` and `HL Single Optyca`.

*@AutoLeading.note: The leading used when `Leading` is `Auto`, as a percentage of the point size; `120` by default.

*@SingleWordJustification.note: How a line holding a single word is set in justified text: `FullyJustified` (spread to fill the line), `LeftAlign`, `CenterAlign` or `RightAlign`.

*@BalanceRaggedLines.note: How the lines of ragged (unjustified) text are evened out, as for a headline: `NoBalancing`, or a shape such as `VeeShape`; a `<Properties>` child.

*@MinimumWordSpacing.note: The narrowest justified text may squeeze a word space, as a percentage of the font's normal space (`80` by default).

*@DesiredWordSpacing.note: The preferred word space, as a percentage of the font's normal space (`100` by default). Unjustified text uses it too.

*@MaximumWordSpacing.note: The widest justified text may stretch a word space, as a percentage of the font's normal space (`133` by default).

*@MinimumLetterSpacing.note: The least space justified text may set between characters, as a percentage of the font's space width; negative values tighten, `0` is the default. Ragged text ignores it.
*@MinimumLetterSpacing.source: InDesign 20.0.1 probe: min/max change nothing in LeftAlign text

*@DesiredLetterSpacing.note: Space added after each character, as a percentage of the font's space width; `0`, the default, adds none. It applies to ragged text too.
*@DesiredLetterSpacing.source: InDesign 20.0.1 probe: 50 adds 2.598 pt per character at 20 pt, half the 5.195 pt space

*@MaximumLetterSpacing.note: The most space justified text may add between characters, as a percentage of the font's space width (`0` by default). Ragged text ignores it.
*@MaximumLetterSpacing.source: InDesign 20.0.1 probe: min/max change nothing in LeftAlign text

*@MinimumGlyphScaling.note: The narrowest justified text may scale its glyphs horizontally, as a percentage; `100`, the default, is the font's own width.

*@DesiredGlyphScaling.note: The horizontal scale of the glyphs, as a percentage; `100`, the default, is the font's own width.

*@MaximumGlyphScaling.note: The widest justified text may scale its glyphs horizontally, as a percentage; `100`, the default, allows no stretching.

*@GridAlignFirstLineOnly.note: When `true`, only the paragraph's first line snaps to the grid set by `GridAlignment`.

*@IgnoreEdgeAlignment.note: When `true`, the paragraph ignores the story's optical margin alignment, so its punctuation is not hung outside the margins.

*@ParagraphDirection.note: The paragraph's writing direction: `LeftToRightDirection`, or `RightToLeftDirection` for Arabic and Hebrew.

*@SameParaStyleSpacing.note: The space between consecutive paragraphs that share this style, in points, in place of their `SpaceAfter` and `SpaceBefore`; `SetIgnore` turns it off.

*@TabList.note: The paragraph's tab stops: a typed `<Properties>` list with one record per stop, each with `Alignment`, `AlignmentCharacter`, `Leader` and `Position`.

*@AllNestedStyles.note: The style's nested styles: a typed `<Properties>` list, one record per nested style with its character style, delimiter, repetition and inclusiveness.

*@NextStyle.note: The paragraph style InDesign gives a new paragraph typed after this one, by its `Self`. It does not change how existing text looks.

*@Hyphenation.note: Whether words in the paragraph may be hyphenated at the end of a line.

*@HyphenationZone.note: In unjustified text, a distance from the right edge, in points, within which a line may end without hyphenating; a larger zone means fewer hyphens.

*@HyphenateAfterFirst.note: The fewest letters a hyphenated word may leave before the hyphen, at the end of the line.

*@HyphenateBeforeLast.note: The fewest letters a hyphenated word may carry to the next line.

*@HyphenateWordsLongerThan.note: Only words with at least this many letters are hyphenated.

*@HyphenateCapitalizedWords.note: When `false`, words that start with a capital letter are not hyphenated.

*@HyphenateLastWord.note: When `false`, the paragraph's last word is not hyphenated.

*@HyphenateLadderLimit.note: The most consecutive lines that may end in a hyphen; `0` means no limit.

*@HyphenWeight.note: From `0` to `10`, the trade between better spacing and fewer hyphens: low values favour even spacing, high values fewer hyphens.

*@HyphenateAcrossColumns.note: When `false`, a word is not hyphenated where the break would carry its end into the next column or frame.

*@KeepWithNext.note: How many lines of the next paragraph must share a column or frame with this paragraph's last line; `0` is off. Typical for headings.

*@KeepLinesTogether.note: When `true`, the paragraph's keep rules apply at column and frame breaks: all lines together, or the counts in `KeepFirstLines` and `KeepLastLines`.

*@KeepAllLinesTogether.note: With `KeepLinesTogether` on: when `true`, the paragraph moves whole rather than breaking across columns or frames.

*@KeepFirstLines.note: With `KeepLinesTogether` on, the fewest of the paragraph's lines allowed before a column or frame break.

*@KeepLastLines.note: With `KeepLinesTogether` on, the fewest of the paragraph's lines allowed after a column or frame break.

*@KeepWithPrevious.note: When `true`, the paragraph's first line stays in the same column or frame as the previous paragraph's last line.
*@KeepWithPrevious.source: dtp; dtp: Keep with Previous paragraph option

*@StartParagraph.note: Where the paragraph starts: `Anywhere`, or at the top of the next column, frame or page, or of the next odd or even page (`NextColumn` … `NextEvenPage`).

*@SpanColumnType.note: Whether the paragraph stays in its column (`SingleColumn`), spans several columns (`SpanColumns`) or splits its column into sub-columns (`SplitColumns`).

*@SpanSplitColumnCount.note: How many columns a span covers, or how many sub-columns a split makes: a typed `<Properties>` child holding a number or `All`.

*@SpanColumnMinSpaceBefore.note: The least space above a spanning or split paragraph, in points; the larger of this and `SpaceBefore` applies.

*@SpanColumnMinSpaceAfter.note: The least space below a spanning or split paragraph, in points; the larger of this and `SpaceAfter` applies.

*@SplitColumnInsideGutter.note: The gutter between the sub-columns of a split paragraph, in points.

*@SplitColumnOutsideGutter.note: The space between a split paragraph's outer sub-columns and the edges of its column, in points.

*@DropCapCharacters.note: How many characters at the start of the paragraph drop; `0` means no drop cap.

*@DropCapLines.note: How many lines tall the drop cap is; `0` means no drop cap.

*@BulletsAndNumberingListType.note: Whether the paragraph is a list item: `NoList`, `BulletList` or `NumberedList`. The bullet or number is generated, never stored in the text.

*@AppliedNumberingList.note: The named list the paragraph's numbering belongs to, a `NumberingList` by its `Self`. A named list can carry the count across stories.

*@BulletChar.note: The bullet: a `<BulletChar>` child with `BulletCharacterType` and `BulletCharacterValue`, the code point in decimal (`8226` for •).

*@BulletsCharacterStyle.note: The character style applied to the bullet, by its `Self`; a typed `<Properties>` child.

*@NumberingCharacterStyle.note: The character style applied to the number, by its `Self`; a typed `<Properties>` child.

*@BulletsTextAfter.note: The text between the bullet and the paragraph's text, in which `^t` stands for a tab; `^t` by default.

*@NumberingExpression.note: The number's text, in which `^#` stands for the number and `^t` for a tab; `^#.^t` by default.

*@NumberingFormat.note: The number style, written as a sample such as `1, 2, 3, 4...`, `I, II, III, IV...` or `a, b, c, d...`; a typed `<Properties>` child.

*@NumberingStartAt.note: The number the count starts at, where the list starts or where `NumberingContinue` is `false`.

*@NumberingContinue.note: When `false`, the count restarts at this paragraph, from `NumberingStartAt`; when `true`, it continues from the previous numbered paragraph.

*@NumberingLevel.note: The paragraph's level in a multi-level list, counted from `1`.

*@BulletsAlignment.note: How the bullet is aligned in the space before the text: `LeftAlign`, `CenterAlign` or `RightAlign`.

*@NumberingAlignment.note: How the number is aligned in the space before the text: `LeftAlign`, `CenterAlign` or `RightAlign`, which lines up numbers of different widths.

*@RuleAbove.note: Whether a rule, a horizontal line, is drawn above the paragraph's first line.

*@RuleAboveColor.note: The swatch the rule above is painted in, by its `Self`. It can also follow the colour of the text.

*@RuleAboveLineWeight.note: The thickness of the rule above, in points.

*@RuleAboveOffset.note: How far the rule above sits above the first line's baseline, in points, measured to the rule's bottom edge.
*@RuleAboveOffset.source: InDesign 20.0.1 probe: 4 pt rule, offset 10: bottom edge 10 pt above the baseline

*@RuleAboveLeftIndent.note: How far the rule above is inset from its left end, in points.

*@RuleAboveRightIndent.note: How far the rule above is inset from its right end, in points.

Color@Visible.note: Whether the colour is listed in the Swatches panel; the reserved process primaries carry `false`. It does not change rendering.

Gradient@Visible.note: Whether the swatch is listed in the Swatches panel. It does not change how anything that uses it looks.

Swatch@Visible.note: Whether the swatch is listed in the Swatches panel. It does not change how anything that uses it looks.

PastedSmoothShade@Visible.note: Whether the swatch is listed in the Swatches panel. It does not change how anything that uses it looks.

Color@Model.note: How the colour prints: `Process` (from the process inks), `Spot` (an ink of its own) or `Registration` (on every plate).

Color@Space.note: The colour space `ColorValue` is in: `CMYK`, `RGB` or `LAB`.

Color@ColorValue.note: The channel values, read as `Space` says: four CMYK percentages, three RGB values from 0 to 255, or L, a and b.

Color@AlternateSpace.note: The space of a spot colour's alternate, such as `CMYK` or `LAB`; `NoAlternateColor` on process colours.

Color@ColorOverride.note: Marks a reserved colour's role: `Specialblack`, `Specialpaper`, `Specialregistration`, `Hiddenreserved`, or `Normal` for any other colour.

Color@TintValue.note: Not how InDesign stores a tint: InDesign drops it and shows the colour at full strength. A named tint is a `<Tint>` element.

ColorGroup@ColorGroupSwatches.note: The group's members as space-separated swatch ids; InDesign's own files list them as `<ColorGroupSwatch>` children instead.

ColorGroupSwatch@SwatchItemRef.note: The swatch this entry puts in the group, by `Self`.

Ink@Frequency.note: The halftone screen frequency of the ink's separation, in lines per inch.

Ink@ConvertToProcess.note: When `true`, the spot ink is output as process inks instead of its own plate.

Ink@PrintInk.note: Whether the ink's separation is printed.

Ink@NeutralDensity.note: The ink's neutral density, which trapping uses to decide which colour spreads into which.

TrapPreset@ObjectsToImages.note: Whether objects are trapped to images.

TrapPreset@InternalImages.note: Whether colours inside an image are trapped to each other.

Font@Version.note: The font's version string, as the font file records it.

Font@DesignAxesName.note: For a variable-font instance, its design axes' names, space-separated, with spaces inside a name written `%20`.

Font@DesignAxesValues.note: For a variable-font instance, its value on each design axis, in the order of `DesignAxesName`.

Image@EffectivePpi.note: The picture's resolution at its placed size, as `(x y)` pixels per inch. Informational.

Image@ActualPpi.note: The picture's own resolution, as `(x y)` pixels per inch. Informational.

Image@Profile.note: The colour profile the picture is handled with, by name, as a typed property.

Link@CanEmbed.note: Whether the linked file can be embedded in the document.
