CellStyle.summary: A named set of cell formatting, such as fill, edge strokes, insets and alignment, that cells and table-style regions apply.

CharacterStyleGroup.summary: A folder of character styles; it organises the panel and changes neither a style's id nor how it inherits.

Color.summary: A colour swatch: its model (process, spot or registration), its colour space and its channel values.

ColorGroup.summary: A folder of swatches in the Swatches panel, listing its members as `ColorGroupSwatch` children; it changes no colour.

ColorGroupSwatch.summary: One member of a colour group, naming the swatch it holds.

Column.summary: One column of a table, named by its index, with its width.

CompositeFont.summary: A composite font: one name that combines faces per script, such as Latin letters from one face and kana and kanji from another.

Condition.summary: A conditional-text condition; text that applies it is shown or hidden with the condition's `Visible` flag.

ConditionSet.summary: A saved combination of condition visibilities, such as a print and a web edition, that can be applied at once.

CrossReferenceFormat.summary: A recipe for the text of a cross-reference, as an ordered list of `BuildingBlock` children.

CrossReferenceSource.summary: The generated words of a cross-reference in a story, naming the format that builds them.

Document.summary: The root of the design map: document-wide settings such as colour profiles, the document-level definitions, and a reference to every part.

EPS.summary: A placed EPS file inside a graphic frame, with its own transform, bounds and link.

Font.summary: One font face the document uses: its family, style, PostScript name, format and whether it was installed.

FontFamily.summary: A font family the document uses, holding one `Font` per face in use.

Footnote.summary: A footnote anchored in the text, holding the footnote's own paragraphs.

GeometryPathType.summary: One contour of an object's outline: its path points and whether it is open.

Gradient.summary: A gradient swatch, `Linear` or `Radial`, with its colour stops as `GradientStop` children.

GradientStop.summary: One stop of a gradient swatch: a colour, its position along the ramp and where the blend before it reaches halfway.

Guide.summary: A ruler guide on a page or spread: its orientation, position, layer and on-screen colour.

Hyperlink.summary: A hyperlink joining a source in the text to a destination, with how its rectangle looks in exported PDF.

HyperlinkPageDestination.summary: A hyperlink destination that is a page of the document, with how a PDF viewer frames it on arrival.

HyperlinkTextDestination.summary: A hyperlink destination that marks a place in the text; InDesign writes it inside the story.

HyperlinkTextSource.summary: The clickable text of a hyperlink, wrapped around the content it covers.

HyperlinkURLDestination.summary: A hyperlink destination that is a web address.

idPkg:BackingStory.summary: The root of `XML/BackingStory.xml`, which holds the backing story of the XML structure; in the design map, the reference to that part.

idPkg:Fonts.summary: The root of `Resources/Fonts.xml`, which lists the fonts in use; in the design map, the reference to that part.

idPkg:Graphic.summary: The root of `Resources/Graphic.xml`, holding colours, gradients, swatches, inks and stroke styles; in the design map, its reference.

idPkg:Mapping.summary: The root of `XML/Mapping.xml`, which maps XML tags to styles; InDesign does not write it, so it appears only in generated files.

idPkg:MasterSpread.summary: The root of one master-spread part, holding one `MasterSpread`; in the design map, the reference to that part.

idPkg:Spread.summary: The root of one spread part, holding one `Spread`; in the design map, the reference to that part, in page order.

idPkg:Story.summary: The root of one story part, holding one `Story`; in the design map, the reference to that part.

idPkg:Styles.summary: The root of `Resources/Styles.xml`, holding the paragraph, character, object, table and cell styles; in the design map, its reference.

idPkg:Tags.summary: The root of `XML/Tags.xml`, the document's list of XML tags; in the design map, the reference to that part.

Image.summary: A placed raster picture inside a graphic frame, with its own transform, pixel bounds and link.

KinsokuTable.summary: A Japanese line-breaking (kinsoku) rule set: the characters that may not begin or end a line, or be split.

Language.summary: A language the document uses, with its quotation marks and its hyphenation and spelling engines.

Link.summary: The link from a placed graphic to its file: the file's URI and format, and whether it is embedded.

MasterSpread.summary: A master spread: pages and items that every body page applying it shows, behind the page's own items.

ObjectStyle.summary: A named set of page-item formatting, such as fill, stroke, corners, effects and text-frame options, that frames and shapes apply.

OpacityGradientStop.summary: One stop of a gradient feather's ramp: an opacity, its position and where the blend reaches halfway.

PageReference.summary: An index marker in the text that contributes its page number to an index topic.

ParagraphStyleGroup.summary: A folder of paragraph styles; folders can nest. It organises the panel and changes neither a style's id nor how it inherits.

PathPointType.summary: One point of a contour: the anchor the outline passes through and the two curve handles at it.

PDF.summary: A placed PDF page inside a graphic frame, with its own transform, bounds, link and page settings.

PDFAttribute.summary: Which page of a placed PDF is shown, which box it is cropped to, and whether its background is transparent.

PreflightProfile.summary: A preflight profile: a named set of rules the document is checked against.

PreflightRuleInstance.summary: One rule of a preflight profile, whether it is switched on, and its parameters.

RootCellStyleGroup.summary: The top of the cell-style tree in `Styles.xml`, holding every cell style and cell-style folder.

RootCharacterStyleGroup.summary: The top of the character-style tree in `Styles.xml`, holding every character style and folder.

RootObjectStyleGroup.summary: The top of the object-style tree in `Styles.xml`, holding every object style and folder.

RootParagraphStyleGroup.summary: The top of the paragraph-style tree in `Styles.xml`, holding every paragraph style and folder.

RootTableStyleGroup.summary: The top of the table-style tree in `Styles.xml`, holding every table style.

Row.summary: One row of a table, named by its index, with its height, its minimum and maximum, and whether it grows with its content.

Section.summary: Where page numbering restarts and how its numbers look: the start page, numbering style, prefix and section marker.

Stripe.summary: One line of a striped stroke style, its position and thickness given as fractions of the stroke weight.

StripedStrokeStyle.summary: A custom striped stroke style made of parallel `Stripe` lines.

Swatch.summary: A swatch entry with no colour values of its own; in InDesign's files it is `Swatch/None`, no paint.

Table.summary: A table in a story: row and column counts, table style, border and dividers, with `Row`, `Column` and `Cell` children.

TableStyle.summary: A named table style: a cell style for each region, plus the table's border, row and column dividers and alternating fills.

TextPath.summary: Type on a path: a story set along the outline of an oval or polygon, with how its glyphs follow the path.

TextVariable.summary: A text variable: computed text such as a running header, the file name or a date, placed in stories as instances.

TextVariableInstance.summary: One placement of a text variable in a story, with the value it showed when the file was saved.

TOCStyle.summary: A table-of-contents recipe: a title, its paragraph style, and one entry per paragraph style to collect.

TOCStyleEntry.summary: One entry of a TOC style: the paragraph style to collect, the style to set it in, its level and its page-number options.

Topic.summary: An index topic: a term the generated index lists, with an optional spelling it sorts under.

TransparencyDefaultContainerObject.summary: The default transparency effects for new objects: four containers (object, fill, stroke, content) with every effect switched off.

TrapPreset.summary: A trapping preset: trap widths, thresholds, and how traps are drawn at joins, at ends and around images.

WavyStrokeStyle.summary: A custom wavy stroke style, its wave size given as fractions of the stroke weight.

XMLElement.summary: One node of the document's XML structure, applying an XML tag to the content it holds.

XmlStory.summary: The backing story of the document's XML structure, holding tagged content that is not placed on a page.

XMLTag.summary: An XML tag the document defines: a name and a colour, applied to content by `XMLElement` nodes.

*@TextWrapMode.note: How text wraps around the object: `None`, `BoundingBoxTextWrap`, `Contour` (around its shape), `JumpObjectTextWrap` (skips past it) or `NextColumnTextWrap`.

*@TextWrapOffset.note: How far text is held off the object on each side, in points: a typed `<Properties>` child with `Top`, `Left`, `Bottom` and `Right` attributes.

*@Inverse.note: When `true`, text flows inside the wrap shape instead of around it.

*@TextWrapSide.note: Which sides of the object text flows along: `BothSides` (the value in every surveyed file), one chosen side, or the side with the largest area.

*@ApplyToMasterPageOnly.note: On a master page item: when `true`, its wrap pushes text only on the master itself, not on the pages that use the master.

ContourOption@IncludeInsideEdges.note: When `true`, text also flows into holes inside the contour, such as the middle of a ring.

*@ContourType.note: Where a contour wrap takes its outline from: `SameAsClipping` (every surveyed file), `BoundingBox`, `DetectEdges`, `AlphaChannel`, `PhotoshopPath`, `GraphicFrame` or `UserModifiedPath`.

*@ContourPathName.note: For a contour wrap from a Photoshop path or alpha channel: the name of that path or channel in the image file.

ClippingPathSettings@IncludeInsideEdges.note: When `true`, contours inside the clipping path become holes, so the area inside a ring is cut away too.

*@ClippingType.note: Where the clipping path comes from: `None`, `UserModifiedPath` (a `PathGeometry` child), `PhotoshopPath`, `AlphaChannel` or `DetectEdges`.

*@AppliedPathName.note: The name of the Photoshop path or alpha channel in the image file that the clipping path comes from.

*@InvertPath.note: When `true`, the inside and outside of the clipping path swap: the area outside the path shows.

*@InsetFrame.note: Shrinks the generated clipping path by this distance, in points; a negative value enlarges it.

*@RestrictToFrame.note: When `true`, the generated clipping path stops at the visible edge of the picture, where the frame crops it.

ClippingPathSettings@Threshold.note: For `DetectEdges`: how dark a pixel may be and still count as background and be clipped away; higher values hide more of the picture.

*@UseHighResolutionImage.note: When `true`, edges are detected from the full-resolution image file rather than its screen preview.

*@FittingOnEmptyFrame.note: The fit applied to a picture placed into the frame, such as `Proportionally`, `FillProportionally` or `FitContentToFrame`; `None` applies none.

*@FittingAlignment.note: The reference point the fitted picture is aligned to, such as `CenterAnchor` or `TopLeftAnchor`.

*@AutoFit.note: When `true`, InDesign fits the picture again whenever the frame is resized.

*@AutoSizingType.note: Whether and how the frame fits itself to its text: `Off`, `HeightOnly`, `WidthOnly`, `HeightAndWidth` or `HeightAndWidthProportionally`. It can shrink as well as grow.

*@AutoSizingReferencePoint.note: The point of the frame that stays fixed while auto-sizing changes its size, such as `CenterPoint` (InDesign's default) or `TopLeftPoint`.

*@FirstBaselineOffset.note: Where the first baseline sits below the top inset: `AscentOffset` (the default), `CapHeight`, `XHeight`, `EmBoxHeight`, `LeadingOffset` or `FixedHeight`.

*@InsetSpacing.note: The space between the frame's edge and its text, in points: a typed `<Properties>` child, one value for all sides or a list of top, left, bottom, right.

*@TextColumnFixedWidth.note: The width of each column, in points, when `UseFixedColumnWidth` is `true`; the frame's width then follows from it.

*@VerticalThreshold.note: With `JustifyAlign` vertical justification: the most space, in points, added between paragraphs before space is also added between lines.

*@MinimumHeightForAutoSizing.note: The smallest height, in points, auto-sizing gives the frame when `UseMinimumHeightForAutoSizing` is `true`.

*@MinimumWidthForAutoSizing.note: The smallest width, in points, auto-sizing gives the frame when `UseMinimumWidthForAutoSizing` is `true`.

*@UseMinimumHeightForAutoSizing.note: When `true`, auto-sizing never makes the frame shorter than `MinimumHeightForAutoSizing`.

*@UseMinimumWidthForAutoSizing.note: When `true`, auto-sizing never makes the frame narrower than `MinimumWidthForAutoSizing`.

*@UseNoLineBreaksForAutoSizing.note: When `true`, auto-sizing widens the frame instead of breaking paragraphs into more lines, where the width can grow.

*@UseFlexibleColumnWidth.note: When `true`, the number of columns follows the frame's width, with no column wider than `TextColumnMaxWidth`.

*@TextColumnMaxWidth.note: With `UseFlexibleColumnWidth`: the widest a column may be, in points; the frame gets as many columns as fit under it.

*@FootnotesEnableOverrides.note: When `true`, this frame's own footnote settings (spanning columns and spacing) replace the document's.

*@FootnotesSpaceBetween.note: With footnote overrides on: the space between consecutive footnotes, in points.

*@FootnotesSpanAcrossColumns.note: With footnote overrides on: when `true`, footnotes in a multi-column frame run across all its columns.

*@ColumnRuleStrokeColor.note: The swatch the rules between the frame's columns are drawn in, by its `Self`.

*@ColumnRuleStrokeTint.note: The tint of the rules between the frame's columns, as a percentage.

*@ColumnRuleStrokeType.note: The stroke style of the rules between the frame's columns, by its `Self`, such as `StrokeStyle/$ID/Solid`.

*@ColumnRuleStrokeWidth.note: The stroke weight of the rules between the frame's columns, in points.

*@EnableOverrides.note: When `true`, the frame's own footnote settings (spanning columns and spacing) replace the document's.

*@SpaceBetweenFootnotes.note: With overrides on: the space between consecutive footnotes, in points.

*@SpanFootnotesAcross.note: With overrides on: when `true`, footnotes in a multi-column frame run across all its columns.

*@UseCustomBaselineFrameGrid.note: When `true`, the frame's text aligns to the frame's own baseline grid instead of the document's.

*@BaselineFrameGridIncrement.note: The spacing of the frame's own baseline grid, in points.

*@StartingOffsetForBaselineFrameGrid.note: Where the frame's first grid line falls, in points from the point set by `BaselineFrameGridRelativeOption`.

*@BaselineFrameGridRelativeOption.note: What the frame's grid start is measured from: the top inset (`TopOfInset`, every surveyed file), the frame's top, the top margin or the page.

*@BaselineFrameGridColor.note: The colour of the frame's own baseline grid on screen.

*@OpticalMarginAlignment.note: When `true`, punctuation and the edges of some letters hang slightly outside the column, so the text edge looks straight.

*@OpticalMarginSize.note: The type size, in points, the optical-margin hang is set for; usually the size of the body text.

*@StoryOrientation.note: The story's text direction: `Horizontal`, or `Vertical` for vertical CJK text.

*@AnchoredPosition.note: How the object is placed: `InlinePosition` (in the line, the default), `AboveLine` (on a line of its own above) or `Anchored` (a custom position).

AnchoredObjectSetting@VerticalAlignment.note: For a custom position: which side of the vertical reference the object goes to, `TopAlign`, `CenterAlign` or `BottomAlign`.

MarginPreference@Top.note: The page's top margin, in points.

MarginPreference@Bottom.note: The page's bottom margin, in points.

*@ColumnGutter.note: The space between the page's columns, in points.

DocumentPreference@Intent.note: The purpose the document was set up for, such as `PrintIntent` for print rather than web or digital use. It does not change the page.

*@PageWidth.note: The document's page width, in points. Each `Page` also carries its own size in its bounds, which can differ.

*@PageHeight.note: The document's page height, in points. Each `Page` also carries its own size in its bounds, which can differ.

*@FacingPages.note: When `true`, pages pair up as left and right pages around a spine, with inside and outside margins.

*@PageBinding.note: Which edge the document binds on: `LeftToRight` (left-edge binding, every surveyed file) or `RightToLeft`.

*@PagesPerDocument.note: The number of pages in the document.

*@DocumentBleedTopOffset.note: The bleed above the page, in points: how far past the trim edge objects print, to be trimmed off.

*@DocumentBleedBottomOffset.note: The bleed below the page, in points: how far past the trim edge objects print, to be trimmed off.

*@DocumentBleedInsideOrLeftOffset.note: The bleed at the inside edge of facing pages, or the left edge of single pages, in points.

*@DocumentBleedOutsideOrRightOffset.note: The bleed at the outside edge of facing pages, or the right edge of single pages, in points.

*@DocumentBleedUniformSize.note: When `true`, the four bleed values are linked and change together.

*@SlugTopOffset.note: The slug area above the page, in points: room beyond the bleed for printer's notes, trimmed off with it.

*@SlugBottomOffset.note: The slug area below the page, in points: room beyond the bleed for printer's notes, trimmed off with it.

*@SlugInsideOrLeftOffset.note: The slug area at the inside edge of facing pages, or the left edge of single pages, in points.

*@SlugRightOrOutsideOffset.note: The slug area at the outside edge of facing pages, or the right edge of single pages, in points. Note the word order differs from the bleed's.

*@DocumentSlugUniformSize.note: When `true`, the four slug values are linked and change together.

*@OverprintBlack.note: When `true`, the `[Black]` swatch at 100 % overprints on output, whatever an object's own overprint setting.

*@ColumnGuideColor.note: The colour of column guides on screen.

*@ColumnGuideLocked.note: When `true`, column guides can't be dragged.

*@MarginGuideColor.note: The colour of margin guides on screen.

*@SnippetImportUsesOriginalLocation.note: When `true`, a placed snippet lands where it was exported from rather than where the user clicks.

*@BaselineStart.note: Where the first baseline grid line falls, in points from the top of the page or the top margin (`BaselineGridRelativeOption`).

*@BaselineDivision.note: The space between baseline grid lines, in points.

*@BaselineGridRelativeOption.note: What `BaselineStart` is measured from: the top of the page or the top margin.

*@BaselineGridShown.note: Whether the baseline grid is shown on screen.

*@BaselineColor.note: The colour of the baseline grid on screen: a swatch or one of InDesign's named interface colours.

*@BaselineViewThreshold.note: The zoom percentage below which the baseline grid is hidden on screen.

*@HorizontalGridlineDivision.note: The document grid's spacing between major gridlines in the horizontal direction, in points.

*@VerticalGridlineDivision.note: The document grid's spacing between major gridlines in the vertical direction, in points.

*@HorizontalGridSubdivision.note: Into how many parts the document grid divides each horizontal gridline interval.

*@VerticalGridSubdivision.note: Into how many parts the document grid divides each vertical gridline interval.

*@DocumentGridShown.note: Whether the document grid is shown on screen.

*@DocumentGridSnapto.note: Whether objects snap to the document grid while being drawn or moved.

*@GridColor.note: The colour of the document grid on screen.

*@GridsInBack.note: When `true`, grids are drawn behind page objects on screen.

*@GuidesShown.note: Whether guides are shown on screen.

*@GuidesLocked.note: When `true`, ruler guides can't be moved.

*@GuidesSnapto.note: Whether objects snap to guides while being drawn or moved.

*@GuidesInBack.note: When `true`, guides are drawn behind page objects on screen.

*@RulerGuidesColor.note: The colour new ruler guides are drawn in on screen.

*@RulerGuidesViewThreshold.note: The zoom percentage below which new ruler guides are hidden on screen.

*@BleedGuideColor.note: The colour of the bleed guide on screen.

*@SlugGuideColor.note: The colour of the slug guide on screen.

*@PreviewBackgroundColor.note: The colour of the pasteboard in Preview mode.

*@MatchPreviewBackgroundToThemeColor.note: When `true`, the pasteboard in Preview mode takes the colour of the interface theme.

*@ShowAllFrameGrids.note: Whether frame grids are shown on screen.

*@ShowAllLayoutGrids.note: Whether layout grids are shown on screen.

*@SnapToLayoutGrid.note: Whether objects snap to the layout grid.

*@ShowCharacterCount.note: Whether frame grids show their character count on screen.

*@UseCircularCells.note: Whether grid cells are drawn as circles instead of squares on screen.

*@EnableLayoutAdjustment.note: When `true`, changing page size, margins or columns moves and resizes objects to keep their places relative to them.

*@AllowGraphicsToResize.note: Whether layout adjustment may resize graphics and groups.

*@AllowRulerGuidesToMove.note: Whether layout adjustment may move ruler guides.

*@IgnoreObjectOrLayerLocks.note: Whether layout adjustment also moves locked objects and objects on locked layers.

*@IgnoreRulerGuideAlignments.note: When `true`, layout adjustment ignores ruler guides when deciding where objects go.

*@SnapZone.note: How close, in points, an object edge must be to a margin, column or guide for layout adjustment to keep it aligned there.

*@EnableAdjustLayout.note: When `true`, changing the page size or margins adapts the page content to the new layout (Adjust Layout).

*@AllowFontSizeAndLeadingAdjustment.note: Whether Adjust Layout may change type size and leading.

*@AllowLockedObjectsToAdjust.note: Whether Adjust Layout also adjusts locked objects.

*@ImposeFontSizeRestriction.note: When `true`, Adjust Layout keeps type sizes between `MinimumFontSize` and `MaximumFontSize`.

*@MinimumFontSize.note: The smallest type size, in points, Adjust Layout may set.

*@MaximumFontSize.note: The largest type size, in points, Adjust Layout may set.

*@HorizontalMeasurementUnits.note: The unit of the horizontal ruler and of horizontal values in InDesign's panels, such as `Millimeters`; the file itself stores points.

*@VerticalMeasurementUnits.note: The unit of the vertical ruler and of vertical values in InDesign's panels, such as `Millimeters`; the file itself stores points.

*@HorizontalCustomPoints.note: The ruler increment, in points, when the horizontal unit is `Custom`.

*@VerticalCustomPoints.note: The ruler increment, in points, when the vertical unit is `Custom`.

*@TextSizeMeasurementUnits.note: The unit InDesign shows type sizes in, such as `Points`.

*@StrokeMeasurementUnits.note: The unit InDesign shows stroke weights in, such as `Points`.

*@PrintDialogMeasurementUnits.note: The unit the Print dialog shows its values in.

*@PointsPerInch.note: The number of points per inch used for unit conversion, normally `72`.

*@CursorKeyIncrement.note: How far an arrow key moves a selected object.

*@GuideSnaptoZone.note: How close, in screen pixels, an object must come to a guide or grid to snap to it.

*@RulerOrigin.note: Where the rulers' zero point is: per spread (`SpreadOrigin`), per page or at the spine.

*@ShowFrameEdges.note: Whether frame edges are shown on screen.

*@ShowNotes.note: Whether editorial notes are shown in the text.

*@ShowTextThreads.note: Whether the threads between linked text frames are shown on screen.

*@SuperscriptSize.note: The size of superscript text, as a percentage of the type size.

*@SubscriptSize.note: The size of subscript text, as a percentage of the type size.

*@SuperscriptPosition.note: How far superscript text is raised, as a percentage of the type size (`33.3` by default).
*@SuperscriptPosition.source: InDesign 20.0.1 probe: 6.66 pt at 20 pt type, 24 pt leading

*@SubscriptPosition.note: How far subscript text is lowered, as a percentage of the type size (`33.3` by default).
*@SubscriptPosition.source: InDesign 20.0.1 probe: 6.66 pt at 20 pt type, 24 pt leading

*@SmallCap.note: The size of synthesised small capitals, as a percentage of the type size, for fonts without real small caps.

*@UseOpticalSize.note: When `true`, text in a variable font with an optical-size axis is set in the instance for its point size; when `false`, the font's default instance.

*@ZOrderTextWrap.note: When `true`, an object's text wrap affects only text beneath it in the stacking order.

*@JustifyTextWraps.note: When `true`, text next to a wrapping object is justified up to the wrap's edge.

*@SmartTextReflow.note: Whether InDesign adds or removes pages as threaded text overflows or shrinks (smart text reflow).

*@AddPages.note: Where smart text reflow adds pages: at the end of the story (`EndOfStory`), the section or the document.

*@DeleteEmptyPages.note: Whether smart text reflow removes pages its text no longer reaches.

*@LimitToMasterTextFrames.note: Whether smart text reflow works only on text frames based on the master's primary text frame.

*@TypographersQuotes.note: Whether straight quotation marks typed in InDesign become typographer's (curly) quotes.

*@LinkTextFilesWhenImporting.note: Whether placed text files stay linked to their source files.

*@ShowInvisibles.note: Whether hidden characters such as spaces, tabs and returns are shown on screen.

*@HighlightHjViolations.note: Whether lines that break the hyphenation and justification settings are highlighted on screen.

*@HighlightKeeps.note: Whether lines that break keep options are highlighted on screen.

*@HighlightCustomSpacing.note: Whether text with custom kerning or tracking is highlighted on screen.

*@HighlightSubstitutedFonts.note: Whether text set in a missing, substituted font is highlighted on screen.

*@HighlightSubstitutedGlyphs.note: Whether glyphs InDesign has substituted are highlighted on screen.

*@BaselineShiftKeyIncrement.note: How far one keyboard step shifts the baseline, in points.

*@LeadingKeyIncrement.note: How much one keyboard step changes leading, in points.

*@KerningKeyIncrement.note: How much one keyboard step changes kerning or tracking, in thousandths of an em.

BevelAndEmbossSetting@Technique.note: The profile of the bevel: `SmoothContour`, `ChiselHard` or `ChiselSoft`.

*@Technique.note: How the glow is built: `Softer` (every surveyed file) or `Precise`.

*@Spread.note: Grows the shadow or glow outward before it fades, hardening its edge, as a percentage of `Size`.

InnerGlowSetting@Spread.note: The glow's choke: moves its edge inward before it fades, hardening it, as a percentage of `Size`.

*@XOffset.note: How far the shadow is offset horizontally, in points; positive is to the right.

*@YOffset.note: How far the shadow is offset vertically, in points; positive is down.

*@Distance.note: How far the effect is offset, in points, in the direction set by `Angle`.

InnerShadowSetting@ChokeAmount.note: Moves the shadow's edge inward before it fades, hardening it, as a percentage of `Size`.

DropShadowSetting@Mode.note: Whether the drop shadow is on: `Drop` when it is, `None` when it is off.

*@HonorOtherEffects.note: When `true`, the shadow follows the shape left by the object's other effects, such as a feather.

*@KnockedOut.note: When `true`, the shadow is hidden behind the object, so it does not show through where the object is transparent.

BevelAndEmbossSetting@Direction.note: Whether the bevel looks raised (`Up`) or sunk (`Down`).

BevelAndEmbossSetting@Depth.note: How steep the bevel's facet is, as a percentage; values well above 100 are allowed.

BevelAndEmbossSetting@Soften.note: Blurs the bevel's shading, in points.

BevelAndEmbossSetting@Altitude.note: The height of the light above the object, in degrees: `0` grazes it, `90` shines straight down.

*@HighlightColor.note: The swatch of the bevel's lit side, by its `Self`.

*@HighlightOpacity.note: The opacity of the bevel's lit side, as a percentage.

*@HighlightBlendMode.note: The blend mode of the bevel's lit side; `Screen` in every surveyed file.

*@ShadowColor.note: The swatch of the bevel's shaded side, by its `Self`.

*@ShadowOpacity.note: The opacity of the bevel's shaded side, as a percentage.

*@ShadowBlendMode.note: The blend mode of the bevel's shaded side; `Multiply` in every surveyed file.

*@InvertEffect.note: When `true`, the satin's light and dark areas are swapped.

*@LeftWidth.note: How far in from the left edge the object fades, in points; `0` keeps that edge hard.

*@RightWidth.note: How far in from the right edge the object fades, in points; `0` keeps that edge hard.

*@TopWidth.note: How far in from the top edge the object fades, in points; `0` keeps that edge hard.

*@BottomWidth.note: How far in from the bottom edge the object fades, in points; `0` keeps that edge hard.

*@FollowShapeMode.note: How the per-side widths follow a shape that is not a rectangle; `LeadingEdge` in every surveyed file.

*@BlendingSpace.note: The colour space transparency is blended in: `CMYK` (nearly every surveyed file) or `RGB`.

*@GlobalLightAngle.note: The document's light angle, in degrees, used by effects whose `UseGlobalLight` is `true`.

*@GlobalLightAltitude.note: The document's light altitude, in degrees, used by bevels whose `UseGlobalLight` is `true`.

*@EnableTransparency.note: Whether the object style sets the basic transparency (opacity and blend mode) at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableDropShadow.note: Whether the object style sets the drop shadow at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableInnerShadow.note: Whether the object style sets the inner shadow at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableOuterGlow.note: Whether the object style sets the outer glow at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableInnerGlow.note: Whether the object style sets the inner glow at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableBevelEmboss.note: Whether the object style sets the bevel and emboss at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableSatin.note: Whether the object style sets the satin at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableFeather.note: Whether the object style sets the basic feather at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableDirectionalFeather.note: Whether the object style sets the directional feather at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@EnableGradientFeather.note: Whether the object style sets the gradient feather at this level; when `false`, an object keeps its own.

*@ClipComplexRegions.note: Whether flattening clips complex areas so the edges between rasterised and vector artwork line up.

*@ConvertAllStrokesToOutlines.note: Whether flattening turns all strokes into filled outlines.

*@ConvertAllTextToOutlines.note: Whether flattening turns all text into outlines.

*@GradientAndMeshResolution.note: The resolution, in ppi, at which flattening rasterises gradients and meshes.

*@LineArtAndTextResolution.note: The resolution, in ppi, at which flattening rasterises line art and text.

*@RasterVectorBalance.note: How much flattening keeps as vectors: from 0, rasterise everything, to 100, keep as much vector artwork as possible.

*@RuleOn.note: Whether a rule is drawn above the first footnote in a column.

*@RuleColor.note: The swatch the rule above the first footnote is drawn in, by its `Self`.

*@RuleTint.note: The tint of the rule above the first footnote, as a percentage.

*@RuleLineWeight.note: The stroke weight of the rule above the first footnote, in points.

*@RuleWidth.note: The length of the rule above the first footnote, in points.

*@RuleLeftIndent.note: How far the rule above the first footnote is indented from the column's left edge, in points.

*@RuleOffset.note: The vertical offset of the rule above the first footnote, in points.

*@RuleType.note: The stroke style of the rule above the first footnote, by its `Self`.

*@RuleGapColor.note: The swatch in the gaps of a dashed or dotted rule above the first footnote.

*@RuleGapTint.note: The tint of the gap colour of the rule above the first footnote, as a percentage.

*@RuleGapOverprint.note: Whether the gap colour of the rule above the first footnote overprints.

*@RuleOverprint.note: Whether the rule above the first footnote overprints.

*@ContinuingRuleOn.note: Whether a rule is drawn above a footnote continued from the previous column.

*@ContinuingRuleColor.note: The swatch of the rule above continued footnotes, by its `Self`.

*@ContinuingRuleTint.note: The tint of the rule above continued footnotes, as a percentage.

*@ContinuingRuleLineWeight.note: The stroke weight of the rule above continued footnotes, in points.

*@ContinuingRuleWidth.note: The length of the rule above continued footnotes, in points.

*@ContinuingRuleLeftIndent.note: How far the rule above continued footnotes is indented from the column's left edge, in points.

*@ContinuingRuleOffset.note: The vertical offset of the rule above continued footnotes, in points.

*@ContinuingRuleType.note: The stroke style of the rule above continued footnotes, by its `Self`.

*@ContinuingRuleGapColor.note: The swatch in the gaps of a dashed or dotted rule above continued footnotes.

*@ContinuingRuleGapTint.note: The tint of the gap colour of the rule above continued footnotes, as a percentage.

*@ContinuingRuleGapOverprint.note: Whether the gap colour of the rule above continued footnotes overprints.

*@ContinuingRuleOverprint.note: Whether the rule above continued footnotes overprints.

*@SeparatorText.note: The text between a footnote's number and its text, such as `^t` for a tab.

*@Spacer.note: The minimum space between the end of the column's text and the first footnote, in points.

*@SpaceBetween.note: The space between consecutive footnotes, in points.

*@FootnoteTextStyle.note: The paragraph style applied to footnote text, by its `Self`.

*@FootnoteMarkerStyle.note: The character style applied to footnote reference numbers in the text, by its `Self`.

*@FootnoteNumberingStyle.note: The number format of footnote references, such as Arabic numerals, Roman numerals or symbols.

*@FootnoteFirstBaselineOffset.note: Where the first baseline of the footnote area falls, with the values of a frame's `FirstBaselineOffset`; `LeadingOffset` in every surveyed file.

*@FootnoteMinimumFirstBaselineOffset.note: The minimum first-baseline offset of the footnote area, in points.

FootnoteOption@StartAt.note: The number the first footnote of the document starts at.

FootnoteOption@Prefix.note: Text placed before each footnote number, such as `[`.

FootnoteOption@Suffix.note: Text placed after each footnote number, such as `]`.

*@ShowPrefixSuffix.note: Where the footnote prefix and suffix appear: on the reference in the text, on the number in the footnote, on both, or nowhere.

*@RestartNumbering.note: When footnote numbering starts again: never, or on every page, spread or section.

*@NoSplitting.note: When `true`, a footnote is never split across columns.

*@EndnoteTitle.note: The heading placed above the endnotes, such as `Endnotes`.

*@EndnoteTitleStyle.note: The paragraph style of the endnotes' heading, by its `Self`.

*@EndnoteTextStyle.note: The paragraph style applied to endnote text, by its `Self`.

*@EndnoteMarkerStyle.note: The character style applied to endnote reference numbers in the text, by its `Self`.

*@EndnoteNumberingStyle.note: The number format of endnote references, such as Arabic or Roman numerals.

*@StartEndnoteNumberAt.note: The number the first endnote starts at.

*@EndnotePrefix.note: Text placed before each endnote number.

*@EndnoteSuffix.note: Text placed after each endnote number.

*@EndnoteSeparatorText.note: The text between an endnote's number and its text.

*@ShowEndnotePrefixSuffix.note: Where the endnote prefix and suffix appear: on the reference, on the endnote's number, on both, or nowhere.

ChapterNumberVariablePreference@Format.note: The number format: `Current` uses the chapter number's own format, or a numbering style such as `UpperRoman`.

PageNumberVariablePreference@Format.note: The number format: `Current` uses the page numbering of the section, or a numbering style such as `UpperRoman`.

DateVariablePreference@Format.note: The date pattern, in date-format tokens such as `MM/dd/yy`.

PageNumberVariablePreference@Scope.note: Whose last page the variable shows: the section's (`SectionScope`) or the document's (`DocumentScope`).

*@IncludePath.note: Whether the file-name variable includes the folder path.

*@IncludeExtension.note: Whether the file-name variable includes the file extension.

*@SearchStrategy.note: Which matching text on the page the running header shows: the first (`FirstOnPage`) or the last (`LastOnPage`).

*@ChangeCase.note: The case change applied to the running header text: `None`, `Uppercase`, `Lowercase`, `Titlecase` or `Sentencecase`.

*@DeleteEndPunctuation.note: Whether punctuation at the end of the running header text is removed.

*@MetadataProviderName.note: The metadata field of the placed image that the caption variable shows.

*@ChapterNumber.note: The document's chapter number, which chapter-number text variables print; 1 when unset.

*@ChapterNumberFormat.note: The format of the chapter number, as a typed `<Properties>` child such as `1, 2, 3, 4...` or `I, II, III, IV...`.

*@ActiveConditionSet.note: The condition set applied last, by its `Self`, or `n` for none. It only records the choice; each `Condition` keeps its own visibility.

*@ShowConditionIndicators.note: How conditional text is marked while editing; with `ShowIndicators` (every surveyed file) the marks show on screen and do not print.

DictionaryPreference@Composition.note: Which hyphenation exceptions text is composed with: `Both` (user dictionary and document), the document's list only (`UseDocument`), or the user dictionary only.

*@MergeUserDictionary.note: Whether the user dictionary's hyphenation exceptions are copied into the document.

*@RecomposeWhenChanged.note: Whether all stories are recomposed when the dictionary changes.

*@ApplyPhotoshopClippingPath.note: Whether the image's own Photoshop clipping path was applied when it was placed.

*@UpdateLinkOption.note: When the placed file is updated: `KeepOverrides` keeps the layer visibility set in InDesign instead of taking the file's.

*@CenterImage.note: Whether data merge centres merged images in their frames.

DataMergeOption@FittingOption.note: How data merge fits merged images to their frames, such as `Proportional`.

*@LinkImages.note: Whether data merge links merged images rather than embedding them.

*@RemoveBlankLines.note: Whether data merge removes lines left empty by empty fields.

*@PreserveAppearance.note: Whether local appearance edits to a linked item survive when its link is updated.

*@PreserveSizeAndShape.note: Whether local size and shape edits to a linked item survive when its link is updated.

*@PreserveInteractivity.note: Whether local interactivity edits to a linked item survive when its link is updated.

*@PreserveFrameContent.note: Whether local edits to a linked frame's content survive when its link is updated.

*@PreserveOthers.note: Whether other local edits to a linked item survive when its link is updated.

*@UpdateLinkWhileSaving.note: Whether linked items are updated when the document is saved.

*@WarnOnUpdateOfEditedPageItem.note: Whether InDesign warns before an update overwrites local edits to a linked item.

*@UpdateWhileSaving.note: Whether linked stories are updated when the document is saved.

*@WarnOnUpdateOfEditedStory.note: Whether InDesign warns before an update overwrites local edits to a linked story.

*@ApplyStyleMappings.note: Whether style mappings are applied when a linked story is updated.

*@RemoveForcedLineBreaks.note: Whether forced line breaks are removed from a linked story when it is updated.

*@IndexFormat.note: How subentries are set: `NestedFormat` gives each its own line; run-in puts them in one paragraph.

*@Level1Style.note: The paragraph style of level-1 index entries, by its `Self`.

*@Level2Style.note: The paragraph style of level-2 index entries, by its `Self`.

*@Level3Style.note: The paragraph style of level-3 index entries, by its `Self`.

*@Level4Style.note: The paragraph style of level-4 index entries, by its `Self`.

*@SectionHeadingStyle.note: The paragraph style of the index's letter headings (A, B, C …), by its `Self`.

*@CrossReferenceStyle.note: The character style of cross-reference prefixes such as See and See also, by its `Self`.

*@CrossReferenceTopicStyle.note: The character style of the topic a cross-reference points to, by its `Self`.

*@IncludeSectionHeadings.note: Whether the index includes letter headings (A, B, C …).

*@IncludeEmptyIndexSections.note: Whether letter headings with no entries are included.

*@ReplaceExistingIndex.note: Whether generating the index replaces the existing one.

*@FollowingTopicSeparator.note: The text between an entry's topic and its first page number.

*@BetweenPageNumbersSeparator.note: The text between an entry's page numbers, such as a comma and space.

*@PageRangeSeparator.note: The text between the first and last page of a page range, such as an en dash.

*@BeforeCrossReferenceSeparator.note: The text between an entry and its cross-reference.

*@EntryEndSeparator.note: The text at the end of each index entry.

IndexingSortOption@HeaderType.note: The script or language group this sort option covers, such as `BasicLatin` or `Russian`.

*@WatermarkDrawInBack.note: Whether the watermark is drawn behind the page content.

*@WatermarkFontFamily.note: The font family of the watermark text.

*@WatermarkFontStyle.note: The face of the watermark text within its font family.

*@WatermarkFontPointSize.note: The size of the watermark text, in points.

*@WatermarkFontColor.note: The colour of the watermark text.

*@WatermarkOpacity.note: The opacity of the watermark, as a percentage.

*@WatermarkRotation.note: The rotation of the watermark, in degrees.

*@WatermarkHorizontalPosition.note: The watermark's horizontal position on the page, such as `WatermarkHCenter`.

*@WatermarkVerticalPosition.note: The watermark's vertical position on the page, such as `WatermarkVCenter`.

*@WatermarkHorizontalOffset.note: Moves the watermark horizontally from `WatermarkHorizontalPosition`, in points.

*@WatermarkVerticalOffset.note: Moves the watermark vertically from `WatermarkVerticalPosition`, in points.

*@AllowTransform.note: Whether an XSLT file transforms the XML during import or export.

*@TransformFilename.note: The XSLT file applied when `AllowTransform` is `true`.

*@CharacterReferences.note: Whether special characters are written as numeric character references in exported XML.

*@ExcludeDtd.note: Whether the DTD declaration is left out of exported XML.

*@ExportFromSelected.note: Whether XML export starts from the selected element rather than the root.

*@ExportUntaggedTablesFormat.note: How tables without tags are exported: as `CALS` tables, or not at all.

*@FileEncoding.note: The text encoding of exported XML, such as `UTF8`.

*@ViewAfterExport.note: Whether the exported XML is opened in a browser afterwards.

*@PreferredBrowser.note: The browser exported XML is opened in.

*@CopyOriginalImages.note: Whether export copies placed images' original files alongside the output.

*@CopyOptimizedImages.note: Whether export copies optimised versions of placed images (converted to web formats) alongside the output.

*@CopyFormattedImages.note: Whether export copies placed images as formatted in the layout (cropped, scaled, rotated) alongside the output.

*@CreateLinkToXML.note: Whether imported XML stays linked to its file so it can be updated.

*@IgnoreUnmatchedIncoming.note: Whether incoming elements that match nothing in the existing structure are left out.

*@IgnoreWhitespace.note: Whether whitespace-only text between imported elements is ignored.

*@ImportCALSTables.note: Whether CALS tables in the XML become InDesign tables.

*@ImportStyle.note: Whether imported XML is merged into the existing structure or appended to it.

*@ImportToSelected.note: Whether XML is imported into the selected element rather than the root.

*@RemoveUnmatchedExisting.note: Whether existing elements with no match in the imported XML are deleted.

*@DeleteElementOnContentDeletion.note: Whether deleting tagged content also deletes its XML element.

*@DefaultStoryTagName.note: The tag given to stories when InDesign tags them automatically.

*@DefaultStoryTagColor.note: The colour InDesign shows the automatic tag for stories in.

*@DefaultTableTagName.note: The tag given to tables when InDesign tags them automatically.

*@DefaultTableTagColor.note: The colour InDesign shows the automatic tag for tables in.

*@DefaultCellTagName.note: The tag given to table cells when InDesign tags them automatically.

*@DefaultCellTagColor.note: The colour InDesign shows the automatic tag for table cells in.

*@DefaultImageTagName.note: The tag given to images when InDesign tags them automatically.

*@DefaultImageTagColor.note: The colour InDesign shows the automatic tag for images in.

*@GIFOptionsPalette.note: The colour palette for images exported as GIF, such as `AdaptivePalette`.

*@GIFOptionsInterlaced.note: Whether images exported as GIF are interlaced, so they load progressively.

*@JPEGOptionsQuality.note: The quality of images exported as JPEG, such as `Medium` or `High`.

*@JPEGOptionsFormat.note: The encoding of images exported as JPEG: `BaselineEncoding` or `ProgressiveEncoding`.

*@ImageConversion.note: The format images are converted to on export: `Automatic` lets InDesign choose, or JPEG, GIF or PNG.

*@ImageExportResolution.note: The resolution of exported images, such as `Ppi150` for 150 ppi.

*@CustomImageSizeOption.note: How exported images are sized: fixed (`SizeFixed`) or relative to the page width (`SizeRelativeToPageWidth`).

*@ImageAlignment.note: How exported images are aligned: `AlignLeft`, `AlignCenter` or `AlignRight`.

*@ImageSpaceBefore.note: Space added above exported images, in the unit set by `SpaceUnit`.

*@ImageSpaceAfter.note: Space added below exported images, in the unit set by `SpaceUnit`.

*@SpaceUnit.note: The unit of `ImageSpaceBefore` and `ImageSpaceAfter`, such as `CssPixel`.

*@UseImagePageBreak.note: Whether exported images get a page break, placed as `ImagePageBreak` says.

*@ImagePageBreak.note: Where an exported image's page break goes when `UseImagePageBreak` is `true`: before it (`PageBreakBefore`), after it, or both.

*@CoverImageFile.note: The image file used as the cover when the cover option names an external image.

*@EpubCover.note: The EPUB's cover: an image of the first page (`FirstPage`), an external image (`CoverImageFile`), or none.

*@ExternalStyleSheets.note: Additional CSS files linked into the exported HTML or EPUB.

*@Javascripts.note: JavaScript files added to the exported HTML or EPUB.

*@BulletExportOption.note: How bulleted lists export: as HTML lists (`UnorderedList`) or converted to text.

*@NumberedListExportOption.note: How numbered lists export: as HTML lists (`OrderedList`) or converted to text.

*@ExportOrder.note: The order content is exported in: the layout's (`LayoutOrder`), the XML structure's, or the Articles panel's.

*@IgnoreObjectConversionSettings.note: Whether objects' own export options (`ObjectExportOption`) are ignored on export.

*@GenerateCascadeStyleSheet.note: Whether a CSS style sheet is generated on export.

*@IncludeClassesInHTML.note: Whether style class names are written into the exported HTML.

*@ViewDocumentAfterExport.note: Whether the export is opened for viewing when it is done.

*@TocStyleName.note: The table of contents style the EPUB's navigation is built from.

*@EpubTitle.note: The title written into the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubCreator.note: The creator (author) written into the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubPublisher.note: The publisher written into the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubDate.note: The date written into the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubDescription.note: The description written into the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubRights.note: The rights statement written into the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubSubject.note: The subject written into the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilitySummary.note: The accessibility summary written into the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilityFeature.note: The accessibility features declared in the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilityHazard.note: The accessibility hazards, such as flashing content, declared in the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilityMode.note: The access modes, such as textual or visual, declared in the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilityModeSufficient.note: The combinations of access modes sufficient to read the EPUB, declared in its metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilityConformsTo.note: The accessibility standard the EPUB claims to conform to, in its metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilityCertifiedBy.note: Who certified the EPUB's accessibility, in its metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilityCredentials.note: The credentials of the accessibility certifier, in the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubAccessibilityReportLink.note: A link to the accessibility report, in the EPUB's metadata.

*@EpubPageRangeFormat.note: Whether all pages are exported (`ExportAllPages`) or only `EpubPageRange`.

*@EpubPageRange.note: The pages to export when `EpubPageRangeFormat` selects a range.

*@EpubSpreadControlOptions.note: How pages pair into spreads in the fixed-layout EPUB; `SpreadsBasedOnDoc` follows the document.

*@BreakDocument.note: Whether the EPUB is split into separate files at paragraphs in the style `ParagraphStyleName`.

EPubExportPreference@ParagraphStyleName.note: The paragraph style at which the EPUB is split into files when `BreakDocument` is `true`.

*@EmbedFont.note: Whether fonts are embedded in the EPUB.

*@IncludeDocumentMetadata.note: Whether the document's own metadata is written into the EPUB.

*@FootnotePlacement.note: Where footnotes go in the EPUB, such as after the story (`FootnoteAfterStory`) or after their paragraph.

*@StripSoftReturn.note: Whether forced line breaks are removed on export.

*@ExportSelection.note: Whether only the selection is exported.

PrintBookletOption@TopMargin.note: The top margin of the booklet's printer spreads, in points.

PrintBookletOption@BottomMargin.note: The bottom margin of the booklet's printer spreads, in points.

PrintBookletOption@LeftMargin.note: The left margin of the booklet's printer spreads, in points.

PrintBookletOption@RightMargin.note: The right margin of the booklet's printer spreads, in points.

*@AltTextSourceType.note: Where the object's alternative text comes from: the XML structure (`SourceXMLStructure`), custom text, or a metadata field.

*@ActualTextSourceType.note: Where the object's actual text for tagged PDF comes from: the XML structure (`SourceXMLStructure`), custom text, or a metadata field.

*@CustomAltText.note: The object's alternative text when its source is custom text.

*@CustomActualText.note: The object's actual text for tagged PDF when its source is custom text.

*@ImageConversionType.note: The format this object is converted to on export, such as `JPEG`.

*@CustomImageConversion.note: Whether this object uses its own image conversion settings on export.

*@EpubType.note: The `epub:type` written for this object in EPUB export.

*@PublishCover.note: The cover of the document published online, such as its first page (`FirstPage`).

*@PublishDescription.note: The description shown with the document published online.

*@PublishFormat.note: Whether the document is published online as single pages (`PublishByPages`) or as spreads.

*@PublishPageRangeFormat.note: Whether all pages are published online (`ExportAllPages`) or only `PublishPageRange`.

*@PublishPageRange.note: The pages to publish online when `PublishPageRangeFormat` selects a range.

*@PublishPdf.note: Whether viewers of the document published online may download it as a PDF.

PrintPreference@Intent.note: The rendering intent used to convert colours when printing, such as `AbsoluteColorimetric`.

PrintBookletPrintPreference@Intent.note: The rendering intent used to convert colours when printing the booklet, such as `AbsoluteColorimetric`.

*@PageRange.note: The pages to print, as a page range.

*@ActivePrinterPreset.note: The print preset the settings come from.

*@Printer.note: The printer the settings are for.

*@PPD.note: The PostScript printer description (PPD) used for output.

*@Copies.note: The number of copies to print.

*@ReverseOrder.note: Whether pages print from last to first.

*@PrintSpreads.note: Whether facing pages print together as spreads.

*@PrintMasterPages.note: Whether master pages are printed instead of document pages.

*@PrintNonprinting.note: Whether objects marked non-printing are printed anyway.

*@PrintGuidesGrids.note: Whether visible guides and baseline grids are printed.

*@PrintLayers.note: Which layers print, such as `VisiblePrintableLayers` (visible layers set to print).

*@PrintFile.note: The file printed to, when printing to a file.

*@Sequence.note: Which pages print: `All`, or only even or odd pages.

*@PrintPageOrientation.note: The orientation on the paper: `Portrait` or `Landscape`.

*@PagePosition.note: Where the page sits on the paper when it is smaller, such as `UpperLeft`.

*@ScaleMode.note: How output is scaled: by the `ScaleWidth` and `ScaleHeight` percentages (`ScaleWidthHeight`) or to fit the paper.

*@ScaleWidth.note: The horizontal print scale, as a percentage.

*@ScaleHeight.note: The vertical print scale, as a percentage.

*@ScaleProportional.note: Whether width and height scale together.

*@Thumbnails.note: Whether several pages print reduced on each sheet.

*@ThumbnailsPerPage.note: How many thumbnails print on each sheet, such as `K1x2`.

*@Tile.note: Whether pages larger than the paper print in tiles across several sheets.

*@TilingType.note: How the tiles are laid out: `Auto` (automatic), automatic justified, or manual.

*@TilingOverlap.note: How much neighbouring tiles overlap, in points.

*@AllPrinterMarks.note: Whether all printer's marks are printed.

*@CropMarks.note: Whether crop marks are printed at the trim corners.

*@RegistrationMarks.note: Whether registration marks are printed, for aligning separations.

*@PageInformationMarks.note: Whether the file name, page number, date and time are printed outside the page.

*@MarkLineWeight.note: The line weight of printer's marks, such as `P25pt` (0.25 pt).

*@MarkOffset.note: How far printer's marks sit from the trim edge, in points.

*@UseDocumentBleedToPrint.note: Whether the document's bleed settings are used when printing instead of this preference's own bleed values.

*@BleedTop.note: The bleed printed above the page, in points, when the document's bleed is not used.

*@BleedBottom.note: The bleed printed below the page, in points, when the document's bleed is not used.

*@BleedInside.note: The bleed printed at the inside edge, in points, when the document's bleed is not used.

*@BleedOutside.note: The bleed printed at the outside edge, in points, when the document's bleed is not used.

*@BleedChain.note: When `true`, the four print bleed values are linked and change together.

*@IncludeSlugToPrint.note: Whether the slug area is printed.

*@ColorOutput.note: How colour is sent to the printer, such as `CompositeRGB`, `CompositeCMYK` or as separations.

*@TextAsBlack.note: Whether all text prints in black.

*@Trapping.note: How trapping is applied when printing; `Off` in every surveyed file.

*@Flip.note: Whether output is mirrored; `None` leaves it as is.

*@Negative.note: Whether output is printed as a negative.

*@PrintCyan.note: Whether the cyan plate is printed.

*@PrintMagenta.note: Whether the magenta plate is printed.

*@PrintYellow.note: Whether the yellow plate is printed.

*@PrintBlack.note: Whether the black plate is printed.

*@CyanFrequency.note: The halftone screen frequency of the cyan plate, in lines per inch.

*@MagentaFrequency.note: The halftone screen frequency of the magenta plate, in lines per inch.

*@YellowFrequency.note: The halftone screen frequency of the yellow plate, in lines per inch.

*@BlackFrequency.note: The halftone screen frequency of the black plate, in lines per inch.

*@CyanAngle.note: The halftone screen angle of the cyan plate, in degrees.

*@MagentaAngle.note: The halftone screen angle of the magenta plate, in degrees.

*@YellowAngle.note: The halftone screen angle of the yellow plate, in degrees.

*@BlackAngle.note: The halftone screen angle of the black plate, in degrees.

*@CompositeFrequency.note: The halftone screen frequency for composite output, in lines per inch.

*@CompositeAngle.note: The halftone screen angle for composite output, in degrees.

*@SimulateOverprint.note: Whether overprinting is simulated in composite output.

*@CRD.note: The colour rendering dictionary used for PostScript output.

*@PostScriptLevel.note: The PostScript language level of output: `Level2` or `Level3`.

*@DataFormat.note: How image data is sent to a PostScript printer: `Binary` or `ASCII`.

*@FontDownloading.note: How much of each font is sent to the printer, such as `Complete`.

*@DownloadPPDFonts.note: Whether fonts already installed in the printer are sent anyway.

*@SendImageData.note: How much image data is sent: all of it (`AllImageData`) or only what the output resolution needs (`OptimizedSubsampling`).

*@BitmapPrinting.note: Whether pages are sent to the printer as bitmaps.

*@BitmapResolution.note: The resolution of pages printed as bitmaps, in dpi.

*@OmitBitmaps.note: Whether placed bitmap images are left out of the output.

*@OmitEPS.note: Whether placed EPS graphics are left out of the output.

*@OmitPDF.note: Whether placed PDF graphics are left out of the output.

*@OPIImageReplacement.note: Whether low-resolution OPI placeholders are replaced with their high-resolution images on output.

*@FlattenerPresetName.note: The transparency flattener preset used when printing.

*@IgnoreSpreadOverrides.note: Whether spreads' own flattener settings are ignored when printing.

*@BookletType.note: How pages are imposed, such as `TwoUpSaddleStitch`; perfect-bound and consecutive layouts are the alternatives.

*@SignatureSize.note: The number of pages in each signature of a perfect-bound booklet, such as `SignatureSize4`.

*@SpaceBetweenPages.note: The gap between the two pages of a printer spread, in points.

*@BleedBetweenPages.note: How far page content may bleed into the gap between the pages of a printer spread, in points.

*@Creep.note: How far pages shift to make up for the thickness of folded paper in a saddle-stitched booklet, in points.

*@AutoAdjustMargins.note: Whether the booklet's margins are set automatically to fit printer's marks and bleed.

*@MarginsUniformSize.note: When `true`, the four booklet margins are linked and change together.

*@PrintBlankPrinterSpreads.note: Whether printer spreads with no content are printed.

CaptionMetadataVariablePreference.summary: The settings of a caption text variable: which metadata field of a placed image it shows.

ChapterNumberPreference.summary: The document's chapter number and its number format, which chapter-number text variables print.

ChapterNumberVariablePreference.summary: The settings of a chapter-number text variable: the number format and the text before and after it.

CjkGridPreference.summary: On-screen settings for CJK layout and frame grids: which grids show and how their cells are drawn. They do not change the page.

ClippingPathSettings.summary: A placed graphic's clipping path: where the path comes from and how it is built.

ConditionalTextPreference.summary: Document settings for conditional text: how condition indicators show and which condition set was applied last.

ContentTransparencySetting.summary: The transparency and effects of a frame's content alone: the text of a text frame or the picture in a graphic frame.

ContourOption.summary: The source of a contour text wrap's outline, such as the picture's clipping path or its detected edges.

CustomTextVariablePreference.summary: The settings of a custom text variable: its fixed text, held as a typed `Contents` property.

DataMergeOption.summary: Data merge settings: how merged images are placed and whether empty lines are removed. They do not change the page.

DateVariablePreference.summary: The settings of a date text variable: the date format and the text before and after it.

DictionaryPreference.summary: How hyphenation uses the user dictionary and the document's own exception list, and whether text recomposes when they change.

DirectionalFeatherSetting.summary: The directional feather effect: each edge of the object fades over its own width.

DocumentPreference.summary: The document setup: page size, page count, facing pages, binding, and the bleed and slug sizes.

DropShadowSetting.summary: The drop shadow effect: a soft, offset shadow cast by the object.

EndnoteOption.summary: The document's endnote settings: numbering, the heading, and the styles of endnote text and references.

EPubExportPreference.summary: Settings for exporting the document as a reflowable EPUB. They configure the export and do not change the page.

EPubFixedLayoutExportPreference.summary: Settings for exporting the document as a fixed-layout EPUB. They configure the export and do not change the page.

FeatherSetting.summary: The basic feather effect: every edge of the object fades over the same width.

FileNameVariablePreference.summary: The settings of a file-name text variable: whether the path and extension are included, and the text around it.

FillTransparencySetting.summary: The transparency and effects of an object's fill alone.

FlattenerPreference.summary: A spread's own transparency flattener settings, used instead of the document's when the spread is printed or exported.

FootnoteOption.summary: The document's footnote settings: numbering, styles, spacing and the rules drawn above footnotes.

FrameFittingOption.summary: How a placed picture fits its frame: the crop on each side, the fit applied and its reference point.

GradientFeatherSetting.summary: The gradient feather effect: the object fades along a linear or radial ramp of opacity stops.

GraphicLayerOption.summary: For a placed file with layers: whether the layer visibility set in InDesign survives when the link is updated.

GridPreference.summary: The document's baseline grid and document grid: spacing, start, colour and whether they show.

GuidePreference.summary: On-screen guide settings: whether ruler guides show, snap, lock or sit behind objects. They do not change the page.

HTMLExportPreference.summary: Settings for exporting the document as HTML. They configure the export and do not change the page.

idPkg:Preferences.summary: The preferences part: the root of `Resources/Preferences.xml`, holding one element per preference, and its `src` entry in the design map.

IndexOptions.summary: The settings last used to generate the index: format, paragraph and character styles, and separators.

InnerGlowSetting.summary: The inner glow effect: a band of colour inside the object's edge.

InnerShadowSetting.summary: The inner shadow effect: a shadow inside the object's edge, as if it were cut out of the page.

LayoutAdjustmentPreference.summary: The layout adjustment settings: whether objects and guides move and resize when page size, margins or columns change.

LinkedPageItemOption.summary: Default options for linked page items: which local edits survive an update and when links update.

LinkedStoryOption.summary: Default options for linked stories: style mapping, line-break handling and when links update.

MarginPreference.summary: A page's margins and column grid; in the preferences, the margins and columns new pages get.

MatchParagraphStylePreference.summary: The settings of a running-header text variable that shows text in a given paragraph style found on the page.

ObjectExportOption.summary: An object's own export options: alternative text, PDF tagging, and how it converts and is laid out in EPUB and HTML.

ObjectStyleContentEffectsCategorySetting.summary: Which effects an object style sets on an object's content; effects it does not set stay as they are on the object.

ObjectStyleFillEffectsCategorySettings.summary: Which effects an object style sets on an object's fill; effects it does not set stay as they are on the object.

ObjectStyleObjectEffectsCategorySettings.summary: Which effects an object style sets on the object as a whole; effects it does not set stay as they are on the object.

ObjectStyleStrokeEffectsCategorySettings.summary: Which effects an object style sets on an object's stroke; effects it does not set stay as they are on the object.

OuterGlowSetting.summary: The outer glow effect: a band of colour around the outside of the object's edge.

PageNumberVariablePreference.summary: The settings of a last-page-number text variable: number format, scope and the text before and after it.

PasteboardPreference.summary: On-screen pasteboard settings: its size and the colours of the bleed and slug guides. They do not change the page.

PrintBookletOption.summary: Settings for printing a booklet: the imposition, the space between pages, creep and margins.

PrintBookletPrintPreference.summary: The print settings used when printing a booklet: printer, marks, colour output and more. They do not change the page.

PrintPreference.summary: The document's print settings: printer, pages, marks, colour output and more. They configure printing and do not change the page.

PublishExportPreference.summary: Settings for publishing the document online: cover, description, page range and layout. They do not change the page.

SatinSetting.summary: The satin effect: soft inner shading made from two offset copies of the object's shape.

StoryPreference.summary: A story's settings: optical margin alignment, text direction and frame type.

StrokeTransparencySetting.summary: The transparency and effects of an object's stroke alone.

TextFramePreference.summary: How a text frame holds its text: columns, insets, vertical justification, first baseline and auto-sizing.

TextPreference.summary: The document's text preferences: superscript, subscript and small-cap sizes, text-wrap rules, smart text reflow and on-screen highlighting.

TextVariablePreference.summary: A generic settings child for a text variable, written by some generators; InDesign writes a typed child for each kind of variable instead.

TextWrapPreference.summary: How text wraps around an object: the wrap mode, the offsets and, for a contour wrap, a `ContourOption`.

TransparencyPreference.summary: The document's transparency settings: the colour space blending happens in and the global light for effects.

TransparencySetting.summary: The transparency and effects of an object as a whole.

ViewPreference.summary: On-screen view settings: measurement units, rulers, frame edges and keyboard increments. They do not change the page.

WatermarkPreference.summary: A watermark InDesign can add to every page: its text, font, position, rotation and opacity.

XMLExportPreference.summary: Settings for exporting the document's XML. They configure the export and do not change the page.

XMLImportPreference.summary: Settings for importing XML into the document's structure.

XMLPreference.summary: Default tags and tag colours for automatic tagging of stories, tables, cells and images, and how tagged content is deleted.
